chapter: Changing styles, the road and nightlife
title: Segregation and lodging on the road in the early 1930s
summary: On early road tours food came by the back door and bands stayed in boarding houses and private homes.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: What were the conditions like on the road in the '20s and '30s and '40s?

Well, the early -- I didn't go on the road until the early '30s. I was on the road in the early '30s. And conditions were pretty bad, you know, during those days. Segregation was real hard, real thick.. And food was hard to get on the road, and you had to go in the back door and things like that for your food; and accommodations were very, very poor. Usually we had to stay in peoples' homes whenever we played little towns or smaller places. We couldn't be accommodated in the hotels. You'd have to go into homes. Some of them would prepare food for you and others wouldn't.
Boarding houses and things like that, right.
But our hours were so irregular. I mean, we'd get in at 2:00 or 3:00 in the morning, and so you would just have to wait until the next morning to eat breakfast, that type of a thing.
